To summarize this incident in one sentence, it is that dangerous technology slipped out of control, ultimately giving rise to disaster... For outsiders, it is undoubtedly a profound lesson. But for researchers, it is instead a revelation, as the potential of Arashi Matter far exceeds our current framework and its potential for development has grown considerably! The secrets of Fregata, the secrets of Shadowrabbit, they may soon be in our grasp. One day, Arashi Matter will also develop to such an extent... And at that time will it, like the ND technology mentioned by Zeke, bring entirely new possibilities to our world, to our future?" —UNCS Researcher's Laboratory Log

profile.label: Research Results
profile.value: An implantable pseudo-neural interface based on nano-scale Arashium Alloy.

profile.label: Warning
profile.value: Do not accept any form of experimental invitation from this individual!

10103153.introduction:
"'Paloma, a genius scientist specializing in the fusion of mechanical and neural medicine, transferred to the Reversion Squad due to a few minor misunderstandings. She is now an indispensable sniper meister, a well-behaved research elite, and Captain Ada's trusted support...'
The above description is a self-report provided by the surveillance target and is of limited reference value. The following supplemental notes are provided accordingly:
1. The target was transferred to the Reversion Squad due to the unauthorized use of Obsidian technology for human modification. To date, she continues to develop portions of the related theoretical technologies.
2. The target demonstrates excellent task completion capability, but frequently acts without authorization, resulting in unnecessary collateral damage.
3. The target has repeatedly accessed critical databases without permission and altered stored data. While the outcomes are often optimized, the scale of these modifications has significantly disrupted subsequent research processes.
Additional note: Statistical analysis indicates that when operating alongside Lieutenant Sapientia, the frequency of the above issues is markedly reduced."—Routine Oversight Committee Report on the Reversion Squad

stories.title: Origin
stories.text:
"Paloma? Of course I remember her. Five years isn't nearly long enough to forget such a peculiar child. When we first met, she was a destitute young girl with no one to rely on, scraping by on government subsidies and a patchwork of part-time jobs just to keep studying. Thankfully, she truly did possess the talent—and the luck—to change her circumstances. Her academic performance and research results stood out sharply among her peers, earning her the attention of the Cognitionis family... yes, that renowned academic family. It sounds enviable, doesn't it? But as I said, Paloma was always an unusual child. She repeatedly refused the Cognitionis family's support and even mocked them to their faces, accusing them of monopolizing research resources and appropriating others' scientific achievements. I remember breaking out in a cold sweat at the time. I was certain her academic career had ended then and there.
Yet her classmate—Sapientia, the eldest daughter of the Cognitionis family—stepped in. She calmed the family's anger and held a long, private conversation with Paloma. I don't know what was said between them. I only know that afterward, Paloma became part of the Cognitionis family, and the two of them gradually grew as close as sisters.
Unfortunately, I retired before they graduated. I only heard that they went through many hardships before eventually heading to Milkhama Island. For researchers, it's a place where risk and opportunity walk hand in hand. I can only hope they're doing well." —Interview with Renowned Neurologist Clay Stig

stories.title: Different Path
stories.text:
"Boss, it's done! Those morons at Cognitionis never realized we replaced the core power unit. Their grand public experiment collapsed in disgrace—and Sapientia was caught in the blast—she even lost her arm. The police? Completely fooled. Took the bait and ran off in the wrong direction. Now all we have to do is— ...Wait. What was that sound? Wh-What are you doing here?! Paloma—how did you fin—ngh!? Aaaah—AAAAAAH!!!
...
...
Heh. The machine's still running. So you can hear me, can't you?
I don't care what your grudge against the Cognitionis family is. I just don't understand this one thing. Why her? Why did it have to be Sapientia? The day before the experiment, she was so excited. She said she finally had the chance to use technology to make this miserable world a little less awful... Of course. Creatures like you would never understand that. So here's the bad news. Thanks to the Obsidian Group's newest breakthroughs, I've already found a way to save her. The technique still needs refinement, though. Which means I need some hardy, long-lasting little lab rats.
You're not trying to run, are you? A rat that escapes the lab isn't a test subject anymore—it's vermin. And vermin get put down."
— Connor & Co. Safehouse No. 3 Communications Log

comment.text: "Obsidian does indeed command technologies that are advanced—and profoundly unsettling—but none of them come without a price... Paloma, even for my sake, you should never have struck a bargain with such demons."

stories.title: Reverse Recruit
stories.text:
"Subject No. 49, Paloma, was arrested and tried a year ago for illegal experiments and intentional harm. Logically, she should have been sentenced to several years in prison, but instead, she was transferred to the Reversion Squad to atone for her crimes. It seems that some influential figures, beyond my reach, have taken a liking to her talents. Coincidentally, the previous squad member who died in action also had the codename 'Paloma'... If this is a joke of fate, it is indeed a dark one.
However, the subsequent period of observation yielded unexpected results. Her actual situation was much better than I initially anticipated. Perhaps it is due to her exceptional ST piloting skills, or maybe it is thanks to the Shelter provided by the current captain, Ada Diaz. She has even become more free and more dangerous... The special forces' authority has given her more opportunities to experiment with those mysterious studies involving arashi material and human integration. Fortunately, this all changed with the recovery and joining of Sapientia Cognitionis—the regular technical exchanges with Obsidian have ceased, and her destructive behavior during missions has been curbed.
Yet, there remains an indelible unease in my heart... In the past, she was willing to use her own right eye as renovation material for experiments. Will she truly give up her research and reform? Perhaps more observation is needed to truly understand this volatile and dangerous genius." —Log of a Senior Agent of the Oversight Committee

stories.title: Pure
stories.text:
"This morning, I received a complaint from the Research Bureau—the third this month... same story as always. Paloma again. This time, she breached the system of the DLAF's 44th Research Institute's system and forcibly initiated an unauthorized live-fire exercise, pitting herself against a swarm of PAMS-equipped test units. The result: more than half of the machines rendered inoperable, and Paloma herself sustaining minor injuries. Fortunately, the combat data proved highly valuable, and Paloma later submitted several concrete and viable proposals for ST improvements. On that basis, the incident was ultimately resolved with nothing more than a formal complaint.
Even after reviewing her past through official records, I still cannot fully understand why she insists on expressing her curiosity toward people—or technology—through such overtly aggressive means... Perhaps that is precisely why she is the most unadulterated among us, and the one best suited to the Reversion Squad." —Excerpt from a report by Leopold Ashford, Vice Captain of the Reversion Squad

10103154.introduction: After the Blair Rebellion, Rosa Díaz reawakened in the Laboratory of the Reversion Squad. Due to radical Experiment plans and intentional external Interference, she experiences some upgrades in memory and self-awareness obstacles. However, she has gained a stronger Arashi Matter resonance ability than before... Although her appearance and demeanor remain unchanged from the past, her way of viewing her companions and her mindset in facing her tumultuous past have quietly changed through interactions with new companions. Now, the only thing Rosa Díaz looks forward to is reclaiming her sister and a reunion and parting with Epiphyllum and that reckless mercenary.

stories.title: Blueprint
stories.text: "Rosa Diaz—the Valkyrie of the UNCS, the blueprint of the Hyper-Aptamer Project, a legend among legends... and yet, in the end, she became someone who sought to shoulder everything, only to be betrayed by everything in return. For her, perhaps death would have been the easier conclusion. Tragically, she was denied even that—true death itself remains beyond her reach. I believe the UNCS—more precisely, the Blair administration—made a grave error in its handling of Rosa Diaz. They were far too eager to convert this heaven-sent creation into immediate combat power, and in doing so, brought about their own backlash... like someone grasping for a blade in haste, only to slice open their own hand. Such incidents are, regrettably, not uncommon within certain internal departments of our own organization. Even so, Rosa's fate should stand as a warning to those who would repeat the same mistake. Therefore, I propose that I personally step forward to establish contact with the other groups currently searching for Rosa Diaz—extending favor where necessary, while securing our objectives in the process." —Excerpt from a meeting recording at Obsidian Headquarters

stories.title: Surpass
stories.text: "I believe our experiment has reached the edge of ethical taboo, as we are creating a new life form that surpasses the realm of humanity. However, the Valkyrie, as a weapon, will still carry human emotions, making her more uncontrollable than any conventional weapon. Therefore, in the subsequent plan advancement, erasing her memory and consciousness should be prioritized. Although we still do not fully understand how human consciousness and memory systems operate, we should at least retain the means to counteract her being out of control... Piloting STs... Since the Valkyrie was born for this, let the ST be her cage." —Internal document from the UNCS Laboratory

stories.title: Determination
stories.text: "After a long and exhausting pursuit, we have finally uncovered new leads—regarding Rosa's whereabouts, and the truth behind the experiment all those years ago... It is now painfully clear that the Dawnstar League is engaged in the very same practices as the UNCS. Once again, we may find ourselves standing against superpowers that control half the world... And if Ada Diaz also chooses to oppose us, then this mission will become even more arduous. I do not expect everyone to involve themselves in a rescue effort with so little hope of success. All of this began because of me and my father; it is a burden that should rightfully be borne by me alone. Therefore, if any of you choose to withdraw at this point, I will hold no one at fault." —Meeting record from GKD Parcel Service

comment.text: "You barely escaped that catastrophe alive, and yet you still insist on throwing yourself back into this disaster... You really do enjoy making trouble for yourself—just like that foolish girl, Sylvie..."

stories.title: Stranger
stories.text: "When she wakes and is forced to face that past, it will be unbearably difficult... facing my existence as well. Watching the person she once tried so desperately to protect become what I am now—will she feel disappointment, regret... or will she do what she always did, blaming everything on herself and bearing fate's imposed burden alone? Heh. I think I finally understand how she felt back then. And yet, even knowing that what I'm about to do runs counter to her wishes, I cannot stand by and watch her continue to wither away. Besides, I am no longer the child who could only hide beneath her protection. I will bring something of sufficient weight to the table—enough to purchase a way to save her—even if that places me on the opposite side of her path... I hope my sister can forgive my stubbornness..." —Communication log from a Dawnstar League laboratory

comment.text: "...Wait for me, Ada. I will get you out of here—no matter what it takes. We'll go home together."

10103155.introduction:
"The DL Oversight Committee was once the laughingstock of all Milkhama. During the war, the military would at times deliberately feed them false intel, knowing the Committee had been thoroughly infiltrated by the GSA. Even their office's weekly meal list became a source of amusement for the opposition.
But everything changed when a man named Colin took over... After a 'purge,' nearly all former members of the Committee vanished, replaced by an 'organization' that officially did not exist.
Much later, the Committee was reestablished. Veronica was the first agent reassigned to Milkhama—marking her as a representative of this new committee.
Decisive, ruthless, and composed under any circumstance, she approaches every situation with unwavering professionalism. She is the model of what an agent should be. But more than that, the reason she was chosen to return to Milkhama Island lies in a recommendation letter from Colin—containing only a single sentence:
'During the war, she found a reason she will never betray.'"

stories.title: Promotion
stories.text:
"I recommend Veronica for promotion to Captain of the 3rd Mobile Unit. She acts decisively and takes care of her teammates... After observing her for the past two years, I believe she has the full capability to take on this position. Haha, she always thinks it's my planning and remote command that allow the team to escape danger time and again, but in reality, her on-the-spot performance is often the key to victory, though she is reluctant to admit it. This humility is also why I recommend her, and I believe her teammates think the same.
That said, there is one thing I am concerned about. Although she always makes firm decisions, if a moment truly comes that demands a heavy sacrifice, can she really make the right call...? Of course, I will do my utmost to prevent such situations from occurring. That is, after all, my duty."

stories.title: Trauma Assessment
stories.text:
"Miss Veronica, you have consistently stated your belief that it was your counterattack that led to the squad's annihilation—even though we all know it wasn't your fault.
For three years, you have repeatedly relived that moment, deliberately ignoring the headquarters' responsibility statement. After leaving the 3rd Mobile, you have refused all joint training exercises. You even insisted on single-handedly transporting the injured to the field hospital, even after your old wounds fared up. Avoiding teamwork like this is precisely what drove you to submit your discharge papers. Your psychological assessment shows that you anonymously remit 80% of your monthly allowance to the families of fallen comrades, yet exhibit pathological pleasure upon receiving returned remittance slips. This self-punishment mechanism is more destructive than any battlefield trauma."

stories.title: Blessing
stories.text:
"We all blame ourselves for everything that went wrong. My way was to seek atonement through sacrifice; hers was to shut herself off completely... Although Veronica says she's fine now and is learning to trust others and be trusted, honestly, I think she still hasn't moved on from that moment.
She has always longed for an answer, and all I can do is give her a speculation to help her not be so tense. But that answer, that... so-called truth, still needs to be discovered by herself."

stories.title: Missions
stories.text:
"The fact that she can bring Sapientia back proves she's more capable than we thought... Although I'm not very fond of surprises, what's done is done—we'd best try to make good use of her.
Being able to easily let go of the obsession that supports her for the rest of her life proves she's the best candidate for that mission—no matter what the final truth is, she will surely be able to accept it."

profile.label: Research Results
profile.value: Arashi Neural Intelligence and Its Differential Evolution Algorithm

10103157.introduction:
The eldest daughter of the renowned Cognitionis academic family, the youngest expert in arashium neural intelligence systems, once regarded by the academic community of the DL as the next rising star after Elise—one who could revolutionize bionic intelligence framework theory. However, due to certain private reasons, she actively joined the Reversion Squad, working as an ST technician on Milkhama Island.
Intelligent and sincere, diligent yet reserved—an unassuming academic type. This is the consensus among her colleagues. But those who know her well dismiss that outright—"Sapi sometimes comes up with ideas even I wouldn't think of, then quietly puts them into action... If you think she's just a well-behaved top student, you'd better be ready for a surprise!"

stories.title: Family
stories.text:
In the DL scientific community, the Cognitionis Family's reputation precedes them. As a historical and influential scholarly family, they possess a vast array of academic, political, and economic resources, which helps them to maintain a long-standing symbiotic relationship with the military-industrial complex. Their position seemed unshakable for years, but all of this changed completely with the development of arashi matter technology. Amidst the intense competition in this emerging field, they lost the upper hand. Now the family needs decisive talent and technology to reestablish authority, and Sapientia, who has shown exceptional talent since childhood, is highly anticipated.
Since she became aware, Sapientia's life has been almost entirely spent in learning. Inundated with study and research, and with all social interactions subject to strict screening by her family, her childhood environment was oppressive and suffocating. To give her some relief, she mustered the courage to tell her first lie. Under the guise of researching Bionic Intelligence Frame technology, she created her own intelligent mechanical friend, Guggle.
As luck would have it, this small act of rebellion brought unexpectedly fruitful results. In the process of continuously modifying and improving Guggle, Sapientia developed a real passion for research, leading her eventually to some remarkable scientific achievements. She soon became a rising star of the DL academic community and even won a place on the most advanced AI Bionics research team at the prestigious Leibniz University. Her life is about to enter a new chapter—away from the family, she can finally break free from long-standing constraints—and will soon meet what turns out to be a lifelong friend.

stories.title: Upheaval
stories.text:
Ever since they first met, Sapientia and Paloma were rivals when it came to tech—a dynamic that did not change even after the two became close friends. This healthy competition only served to amplify her passion and natural talent. Inspired by Paloma's pseudo-neural components, Sapientia successfully developed a brand-new differential evolution Bionic AI modeled after Guggle. The Cognitionis family were ecstatic, but from others it attracted animosity.
In September, XC 116, a severe accident of unknown origin occurred during a public experiment at Leibniz University, resulting in the loss of Sapientia's left arm. For her protection and to facilitate an investigation, the family chose to isolate her, cutting off contact with the outside world. Aside from her family and designated medical staff, Guggle was once again her only companion.
However, this closed treatment did not yield the expected results—due to arashi particle contamination from the accident, the muscles on Sapientia's left side suffered a degree of atrophy, and her recovery was painfully slow. The residual arashi particles obstructed neural signals, rendering existing prosthetic limbs ineffective. 
As a month passed, Sapientia's spirits continued to sink... It was then that a special envoy from Obsidian suddenly appeared in the ward, bringing advanced prosthetic technology and new medical treatments—along with the news that Paloma had been arrested and imprisoned for illegal experimentation and intentional injury.

stories.title: Abyss
stories.text:
Having just adapted to her new prosthetics, Sapientia applied to join the Reversion Squad—a move the Cognitionis family naturally opposed. Sapientia, however, had already prepared a convincing excuse—Milkhama Island is the source of arashi matter and the cutting-edge testing ground for the Bionic Intelligence Frame. Only there can she truly perfect her technology and maintain the family's academic prestige.
It didn't take long for Sapientia to first set foot on Milkhama with Guggle in tow. But when she disembarked, what awaited her was not her long-missed friend, but the contact from Obsidian headquarters. As the price for stopping the ongoing collaboration between Paloma and Obsidian, Sapientia was forced to become an informant within the Reversion Squad, tasked with providing regular test data on Ada.
She resisted, almost subduing the Obsidian contact, but her prosthetic suddenly went out of control due to a backdoor command left by the contact. Only then did she realize this had all been a trap from the start. Now, struggling to maintain a facade of calm while desperately searching for a way out, Sapientia anxiously awaited a new opportunity.
Whether by luck or misfortune, this opportunity soon materialized: the Reversion Squad took on Rosa Diaz—someone whose value to Obsidian far outweighed that of both Sapientia and Paloma combined.

comment.text: Sapi, you idiot!!! Why didn't you explain it to me earlier!!

stories.title: Daybreak
stories.text:
Through the concerted efforts of many, the Reversion Paradox centered around Rosa Díaz ultimately avoided its worst-case scenario. However, the Oceanic Conclave was never going to remain indifferent. A joint investigation task force, formed by the Oversight Committee and the Defense Force Headquarters, intervened and ordered Veronica to escort Sapientia—the direct instigator of the incident—to their base for interrogation.
Despite this, Sapientia felt a sense of clarity she hadn't known for a long time. The nanobots implanted in her prosthetics had been destroyed by the power of the Hyper-Aptamer, and Obsidian had lost its leverage over her and Paloma. Following the upheaval, the members of the Reversion Squad finally opened up to one another, and the six, each of whom had started with their own hidden agendas, were now gradually moving toward the same destination, together... Sapientia no longer needed to force herself to make impossible sacrifices; her only focus now was protecting this hard-won home and helping Ada and Rosa break free from the shackles fate had imposed upon on them. 
This is her atonement for the past—and her hope for the future.

comment.text: Though she's weak, lying on the hospital bed, she still seems much more at ease... Perhaps for her, life is only just now beginning.

profile.label: Original Unit
profile.value: Landing Force Assault Special Operations Team (Disbanded)

10103158.introduction: "Wyatt Morgan? Of course I know him, 'Ace of the Joint Mobile Battalion,' 'Hero of the Milkhama War'... His titles before retirement were more impressive one after another, but people in our line of work prefer to call him 'Cowboy.' You might have heard the saying—strong, smart, cautious, lucky... At least possessing one of these traits can help you survive longer on the battlefield. And him? He is a lone wolf, yet he survives better than most, returning intact from any kind of hell. Although I don't know why such a talented person would give up a promising future to become a mercenary, the fact proves he is indeed cut out for it, and given time, he will surely become a new legend in the mercenary world. It's a pity, though, that I heard he was recently recalled by the NDF to Milkhama Island, and that's not good news. Those in the know understand that place seems peaceful on the surface, but in reality, it's a slaughterhouse where big shots incubate wars and reap the profits. I don't know what considerations led him to accept this task..." —Interview with a Certain Mercenary Contactor

stories.title: Youthful Bravado
stories.text:
Even before enlisting, Wyatt Morgan was already something of a local legend. All it took was a late-night dare: sneaking alone into the barracks command building and covering the walls with graffiti. Had he not run straight into the newly appointed commander, Blair Bluecher, on patrol, he might have walked away unscathed. Even so, headlines about a "sixteen-year-old breaking into the barracks" humiliated the NDF. Soon after, the rebellious boy vanished from the streets, and most assumed he had been severely punished—until months later, when he returned on leave wearing the uniform of Enfield Military Academy. Only then did people realize the outcome had been anything but dire. Blair had recognized his sharp mind and not only spared him punishment, but personally recommended him for academy admission.
Perhaps it was fate. In Wyatt's first year, the armored training program underwent reform. The unprecedented new system—the ST—was introduced as a core discipline for all soldiers. Veterans and recruits alike started from zero, learning together. Wyatt's aptitude stood out almost immediately.
Three years later, upon graduating with exceptional marks, Wyatt received an urgent transfer order. He was assigned to the Landing Force mobile battalion under Blair's command, bound for Milkhama Island to protect commercial partners and confront the DL.

stories.title: Ace's Desolation
stories.text:
"Ace Pilot." The title arrived after Wyatt completed his thirty-seventh sortie. Unlike William, who led the main force head-on, Wyatt's special operations unit specialized in maneuver warfare, striking key DL nodes from their weakest points. His successes made him a thorn in the DLAF's side. Repeated targeted encirclements failed to kill him—or even slow his momentum. Promotions followed in rapid succession: Second Lieutenant, Lieutenant, Captain. Many believed he would reach Major before William. All of that ended with the sudden conclusion of the war.
The surprise assault on Milthus—an operation intended by the NDF to pressure Obsidian—was vehemently opposed by Wyatt. He warned that such short-sighted action would drive the NDF into disaster. Blair ignored him, gambled everything, and inadvertently triggered the Milthus explosion that reshaped the conflict. From that point on, the rift between them could no longer be repaired. Years later, with military backing, Blair became Viceroy of West Milkhama and once again summoned his former subordinate. This time, Wyatt refused. He abandoned his honors, left the army, and became a free mercenary.

comment.text: I grew up watching Uncle Wyatt fight under my father's command. He took care of me more times than I can count. Back then, I never imagined the two of them would end up so divided. Now... I think I understand a little.

stories.title: Lone Cowboy
stories.text:
Wyatt's mercenary career unfolded more smoothly than he had imagined. Whether due to his combat experience, command instincts, or simply his calm, perceptive nature, he adapted effortlessly. For nearly a decade, he crossed battlefields and walked away alive, earning a reputation as a legend. People remembered not just his skill, but his solitary, easygoing nature. Gradually, his real name faded, replaced by a single moniker: "Cowboy."
That freedom didn't last. In December of XC 118, an agent from the UNCS intelligence division found him and delivered news from Milkhama Island—Blair's downfall, the NDF's decline, the DLAF's rise. The military needed someone to replace Blair and William, to reorganize the West Milkhama NDF and keep its last embers alive. Wyatt gave no answer. He drank in silence until he passed out.
No one knows what he decided that night. Only that afterward, the mercenary Cowboy vanished—and the NDF regained its former ace.

stories.title: Army's Hope
stories.text:
After returning to Milkhama, Wyatt delayed executing his orders. For nearly half a month, he moved in secret, assessing the island firsthand. Much had changed, but the growing stench of gunpowder between factions was familiar—a prelude to war. Worse still, the battered NDF was clearly unprepared for what was coming.
As tensions escalated in the Central Mining Area and GSA oversight faltered, Wyatt seized the moment. He led military agents to remove parliamentary officers obstructing NDF operations and quickly rallied veterans disillusioned with the current state of affairs. Acting as both a voice for the rank and file and a proxy for high command, the burden he carried far exceeded expectations.
"Being a mercenary was a hell of a lot freer than this damned Lieutenant Colonel gig." He muttered variations of that curse several times a day. Even so, he had no intention of walking away. Since he had chosen to return to this hell, he would see it through—to win the coming war, or at the very least, ensure that as many comrades as possible survived.

10103159.introduction: "Adele Martin finally agreed to meet me—at her private winery. To cater to her taste, I brought a few bottles of treasured wine upon departure, and Adele praised them highly, personally storing them in her cellar. At the time, I thought it was a good start; although gaining Adele's favor was no easy task, at least she didn't throw me out at first sight. We did a lot of preparation to secure Harpy's funding, and Adele expressed her approval. However, Harpy's assessment of a new team's capabilities is extremely strict, and I must admit Adele's professionalism, knowing how to make a rejection that allows both parties to maintain dignity. Failing to gain Harpy's support, my team gradually fell into low spirits, forcing us to risk it all by taking on dangerous tasks. They were far beyond our ability to handle, and we nearly faced total annihilation. But the unexpected happened; amidst a siege, I saw the late-arriving Adele, who shielded me from artillery, congratulating me on passing the final test. From then on, Harpy would be our most solid industrial supporter... It turns out she had been closely monitoring us during our struggling days. For some reason, seeing her beautiful smile, a chill rose in my heart. The most solid backer also seemed like the hardest mire to escape." —A Burned, Anonymous Memoir

stories.title: Elegant Walker
stories.text:
"The new commissioner was stunning, effortlessly capturing everyone's attention as she stepped into the office hall. Naively, I thought she was just here as the spokesperson for some mercenary team to discuss business, and I wondered how such a captivating type could appear among mercenaries. It wasn't until she made her way through the crowd to greet me that I realized Adele Martin, this radiant woman, was going to work with me.
Before her, most of the commissioners I encountered had an elite demeanor, always in perfectly tailored suits, with impeccable hairstyles, and a black briefcase that never left their side, ready to make a perfect appearance at any time of the day. But Adele was different. She was a refined woman with high standards for quality of life. Even during urgent missions, if you approached her during break time, you had to patiently wait for her to finish yawning lazily before discussing business. However, this didn't mean she was unprofessional. On the contrary, it was her meticulous planning and calculations that allowed her to have a peaceful break even during urgent missions.
I was curious about the background of this beautiful lady. After several collaborations and becoming familiar with each other, we talked about the past over a drink one time. She poured me a glass of red wine, a specialty from her hometown—one of them, as I knew her hometown Belvino was also the world-renowned perfume capital. It turned out she came from such an elegant and romantic place, though I didn't know why she was now in Milkhama. When we touched on this topic, she looked out the window and gradually fell silent... Perhaps there's a more intricate story behind it? I didn't say anything further, just gently clinked my glass against hers." —Excerpt from the musings of a former employee of Harpy Trading

stories.title: Nonconformity
stories.text:
"Andy, lately I've been feeling uneasy, and Adele might have already sensed something is wrong. Some time ago, she inquired about the management situation at Franchet, and since then, she's often been out and about, perhaps trying to ease our burden... Ah, Andy, I think the day we've foreseen has finally come.
In the blink of an eye, eight years have passed. The frail girl rescued from the fire eight years ago has now grown into a graceful young lady. I've always emphasized to you that Adele is the most special child in Franchet. This uniqueness is not just about her distinctive appearance, but also her overly sensitive personality. I don't know what kind of education she received from her parents before, but judging by her keen observation skills, precocious thinking, and knowing how to make her life better, perhaps she has endured many hardships in the past...
Franchet was initially established to provide a shelter for children who lost their loved ones, without expecting anything in return. Moreover, Adele is still a child, and she has her own, longer path ahead, and shouldn't stop for Franchet.
Andy, I've heard that you are now teaching at the business school. Could you write a letter of recommendation for Adele, so she might qualify for an exceptional admission review? If you have any doubts, you can come back and meet the child—she certainly won't disappoint you." — Handwritten letter record by the director of Franchet Orphanage

stories.title: Radiant Star
stories.text:
"Adele Martin? Heh. Of course I know her—the new favorite Saliman's been grooming lately. She's constantly accompanying her to seminars. Someone even spotted her at Mr. Huber's charity auction last time. Why, you ask? Frankly, I'm curious myself what she did to earn Saliman's attention straight out of graduation. But for us, that's beside the point. This is a signal. A critical one. Saliman may already be laying the groundwork for her next commercial expansion, and Adele Martin is just one small piece of that puzzle.
You'd do well to make her acquaintance. Anyone who catches Saliman's eye has to be exceptional in some way. While you're at it, find out whether Saliman really intends to extend her reach to Milkhama Island. I have a feeling her recent moves are based on new intelligence. What's the difficulty in socializing? Invite her out for a few bottles of good wine in my name. She's from Belvino, isn't she? The wine I have here is something even Saliman still talks about. She won't dislike it." —Recorded call with a senior executive of a corporate group

stories.title: An Answer
stories.text:
"Before leaving Harpy for good, I followed Adele on one last mission. It took place in Thepia, assisting 'Roaring' in a stronghold seizure.
Roaring was a mercenary group Adele had believed in from the beginning. We tracked several of their operations, and she praised them as disciplined and unyielding. What they lacked wasn't resolve, but funding and equipment. Adele devised a rigorous evaluation plan, and after they passed, entered into a long-term partnership with them. In the end, they were annihilated by Thepia's artillery. Adele wasn't surprised. Milkhama has no shortage of mercenary groups, and no one remains undefeated forever. She calmly laid a wreath for Roaring's commander, her eyes utterly still. ...but I was not the same.
Even now, I can't remember how I survived that inferno. The pain from the shellfire still blurs my senses at times. The one thing I know for certain is that Adele never left my side—she led me through the flames to safety. Some people pass through gunfire and are left with fear, never wanting to smell smoke again. Others see it as a baptism—each trial by fire a rebirth. Adele and I were always different in that way. Now I'm writing these notes on a distant continent, while Adele continues chasing her goals on that island of endless conflict. Where does her road end? Does this life truly bring her peace? I don't know. Perhaps... only she does." —Excerpt from the essays of a former Harpy employee

comment.text: There's nothing simple about Adele. Whatever she's seeking, we must be careful and absolutely avoid becoming tools for her gain.

10103161.introduction: "Zoey Steele, adjutant to Colin, Executor of the Oceanic Conclave, is responsible for assisting in the execution of classified operations. She is known for her volatile temperament and decisive actions, adhering firmly to a survival-of-the-fittest philosophy. She actively seeks out challenges against stronger or higher-ranking individuals in order to elevate her position within the 'food chain.' Despite her considerable strength, such traits make her ill-suited for the role of adjutant. As her personal file remains sealed, the exact circumstances of her association with the Oceanic Conclave cannot be confirmed. However, there are rumors that she once launched an armed assault on Dawnstar League officials and later engaged in direct combat with Colin's forces. If these claims are accurate, her relationship with Colin warrants reassessment to avoid potential misjudgment in future engagements." —Oversight Committee Internal Report

stories.title: Raid
stories.text:
The 225th Special Operations Training Camp is a talent cultivation institution directly managed by the Operations Department under the Oceanic Conclave of the DL. It periodically recruits individuals with special talents from across the country, training them to become the sharpest blades of the Oceanic Conclave. In XC 112, Zoey Steele, only seventeen years old, became one of its students. No one knows how she got in, least of all her classmates or the Oversight Committee. 
The only certainty is that this girl possesses astonishing talent. In her first melee training class, she nearly pierced a classmate's throat with a dagger, and in the subsequent simulated ST battles, she held her own against the instructor. She thus became a celebrity in the camp, gradually integrating into the environment. However, people never understood the source of the burning hatred in her eyes until the attack two years later—Colin Doyle, as a special envoy of the Oceanic Conclave, was on an inspection tour when he was targeted in his own room by a bomb attack and a knife-wielding assassin—and that assassin was none other than Zoey.

stories.title: Objective
stories.text:
With Zoey's capture, some well-informed trainees finally learned about her past.
She was born into a southern mercenary group native to the DL, and once followed her father, the mercenary group leader, in an attack on high-ranking DL officials. However, due to Colin's timely support, the attempt failed, and her father died in the fierce battle that ensued. After the battle, Zoey, as the sole surviving member, was taken prisoner. Colin didn't mistreat her, but neither did he release her—instead, after a conversation, he suggested she join the 225th Special Operations Training Camp.
"I'll grow stronger. And once I do, I'm coming for you, Colin Doyle."
"If I had a dime for each time I've heard that... Yet here I am, alive and kicking. But if that's what you need to keep on keeping on, be my guest."
Years later, the exchange was reprised, this time with smoke and steel.
Zoey, however, failed to achieve her goal. Colin, though his face was blackened from the smoke and soot, escaped unscathed, parrying all of Zoey's follow-up attacks until she was apprehended by guards. 
Perhaps due to Colin's moves behind the scenes, the serious charge of assassinating an officer was eventually lowered to the misuse of explosives and destruction of public property. After a month's confinement, Zoey returned to the training camp, catching up with her final test as a trainee.

stories.title: Directive
stories.text:
Upon leaving the training camp, Zoey was immediately recruited by the operational department under the Oceanic Conclave and subsequently participated in over twenty special action missions. Although not all the missions ended smoothly, her well-honed combat skills were recognized, especially her ability to operate STs in solo combat, which rivals that of the military elite. If it weren't for her record of attacking a superior officer, she might have become an executor of the Oceanic Conclave.
Until XC 116, the situation on Milkhama Island accelerated into turmoil due to the White Maple incident, prompting the Oceanic Conclave to dispatch multiple teams of agents to gather intel in Milkhama, leaving some local positions vacant. This allowed the outstanding Colin to gain more authority. In this context, Zoey regained the Oceanic Conclave's attention, with Deputy Secretary McGonagall personally meeting her to convey a top-secret order—embed herself in Colin's team, watch him and keep him in check, all with authorization for independent action if necessary.
Zoey quickly understood the intention behind this; it was a clear warning from the Oceanic Conclave to Colin. Harnessing her grudge, she would be the Sword of Damocles held over Colin's head.

stories.title: Chance
stories.text:
Colin seemed to have anticipated Zoey's arrival, even holding a makeshift welcome party. Naturally, Zoey returned his hospitality with an immediate attack. Colin again frustrated her attempt, blocking her just like last time. But Zoey restrained herself. She understood that she would have countless opportunities to achieve her goals, while Colin could not afford to slip up even once. Despite their twisted superior-subordinate relationship, their cooperation during missions was surprisingly good. Even though Zoey did not always obey Colin's orders, the results still perfectly realized his overall tactics, clearing countless obstacles from the frontlines.
After the Milkhama Central Mines incident in March of XC 119, the Oceanic Conclave urgently needed a strong agent to go to Milkhama to maintain the situation and recover the key results of the Nova Project. Colin was the only man for the job. Whether through a direct clash with a Super Pilot or Colin finally showing a crack under high pressure, these were opportunities Zoey had been hoping for. Thus, she did not hesitate to follow him on the mission, setting foot on the land she had never known.
"This time, I'll prove I'm no pushover."

10103162.introduction:
"Colin Doyle, former Milkhama landing forces ace pilot, commander of the Special Operations Team directly under the Dawnstar League Armored Forces General Staff. During the war, he operated extensively in West Milkhama, conducting behind-enemy-lines missions that caused significant disruption to the UNCS. After returning to the front, he personally led his forces in multiple key engagements, including the Battle of Milthus... The old fox truly is what he claims—a 'war hero.' But believe me, he's not someone you want to deal with.
Most people have an inner anchor—something that defines who they are and guides their actions. Find that anchor, and you find a way to handle them. He's different. Yesterday, he'd take a bullet for a comrade. Today, he could send that same person to trial. Tomorrow, he might present evidence to overturn the verdict. Even after four years working with him, I still can't tell what his anchor is... or if he has one at all. Any interaction with him is inherently unequal. Of course, if you're not his enemy—or if you don't mind your secrets being completely transparent—then just follow his orders. That's the only way to ensure the mission gets done." —Statement by a Colonel Staff Officer of the Armed Forces

stories.title: Emerging Edge
stories.text:
"That kid Colin is here again. Seems this time he fell asleep during sniper training and left his radio on... Broadcast his own snoring to HQ for a good half hour... Honestly, I'm somewhat impressed by him. He's been penalized four times in two months. If it were anyone else, they'd have been kicked to the curb long ago. But this kid's training results... the officers turn a blind eye. But he can't just get off scot-free; his reward for last week's tactical exercise was revoked, and I've got him doing grunt work for a week. Just as well, the military recently brought in some new gadgets modified from bipedal construction rigs... "STs" I think those Milkhama folks call them. I didn't think I'd have anyone to test them for me.
To be honest, I thought Colin would just slack off, but you should've seen his eyes light up when he saw those things. He kept pestering me about them—first time I've seen him really enthusiastic about something. Turns out that when this kid encounters something he's into, he's like a whole other person. He finished a full day's basic testing in just three hours. Before this, the largest machinery he had operated was a troop transport.
If the military's plan for large-scale ST deployment goes ahead, Colin's gonna turn some heads, believe you me. Provided he doesn't step on too many toes, that is..." — Maintenance Squad Leader's Log

stories.title: Elite Espionage
stories.text:
"Yes, I fought in Captain Colin's team for nearly a year. We infiltrated West Milkhama to collect intel and faced off against the NDF's STs together... I may sound proud of it all now, but to be honest, at first I didn't trust him one bit. We were both in our twenties, but he was a soldier trained to operate STs, while I was a professionally trained agent from the intelligence bureau. Why should he lead me?
But that attitude didn't last long. As the battles intensified, our situation behind enemy lines became increasingly dangerous. The pressure of being suspected, arrested, or even killed almost crushed me, yet he continued to eat, sleep, and mingle with famous figures from both sides, perfectly playing the character of a carefree merchant in the NDF's territory. It was thanks to him we survived the most danger period. We even uncovered the NDF's plan to bypass the Mouty Mountains Region for a surprise attack, preventing disaster and earning us the title of heroes among the few who knew... To me, it was the pinnacle of my career—for him it was just a prologue.
Just as our infiltration mission was about to end and we were preparing to retreat to East Milkhama, we ended up with William on our tails—yes, that William, William Stein, ace pilot of the NDF. I thought I was done for, but Colin managed to drive him off with a series of improvised traps and a stolen ST. It was then that I realized what being an elite soldier really means." — A DL intelligence officer recounts post-war

stories.title: Nova Project
stories.text:
"The hero Colin did not accept Officer Tiphys's invitation, giving up the opportunity to become a DLAF commander. It's not that surprising—after all, having skill at commanding doesn't mean you necessarily want to stay on the battlefield. I've heard him complain more than once to those around him about the burdens of being an ace pilot. To him, getting time to put his feet up takes priority... It seems silly, but that's how he really seems to feel. This is why I'm shocked by what's happened to him—I never would've guessed he'd join the Oceanic Conclave Executor force, exercising all that authority on behalf of those big shots, even fully taking over that highly confidential 'Nova Project'... Has his mindset really undergone such a profound change, or did I misjudge him from the start?
In any case, after taking office, he significantly revised the original plan of the Oceanic Conclave, rearranged the team, and persistently pulled a large amount of resources from the logistics and R&D departments. He clearly had his own vision. As far as I know, he indeed accomplished what may be the greatest achievement in East Milkhama—you guessed it, that "Super Pilot," cultivated by that very Nova Project.
Having accomplished such a great feat, Colin was quickly transferred to the homeland. I guess he's doing very well for himself... Well, it's hard to say, because as outstanding as his abilities are, he has an equal talent for getting on people's nerves."—Communication Log of a retired DLAF Officer

stories.title: Executor
stories.text:
"Colin Doyle, effective immediately, you are granted special freedom of action to return to Milkhama and execute this critical mission. You have three objectives: first, receive the Nova Project subject research result A-00 and subdue Ada Diaz; second, directly oversee DL political affairs and thoroughly investigate the connection between Governor Lukmund and the current chaos; third, suppress the UNCS's political expansionism and take control the situation in East Milkhama."
"Straight to the point as always... Understood, I'll depart tomorrow."
"If there's anything you need, say it now. This is a long-term mission, and we will continue to provide assistance."
"Hmm... Oh right, include Zoey as well, I'll take her to see the world."
"Zoey Steele? Are you sure she won't get in the way of your mission?"
"Don't worry, she won't. I trained her personally. She's different from those guys on the island—she's got sharp instincts... Though, just for insurance, I want advance clearance to call in some DLAF heavy hitters."
"We aren't looking for a shooting war, Colin."
"Naturally, but being ready for one wouldn't hurt... After all, for all we know, the whole of Milkhama may be looking to pick a fight with us."
—Oceanic Conclave Critical meeting Record fragment
